reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch note the herem left survivors, since Amalekites reappear later, and that Agag was a dynastic title for Amalekite kings, not one man's personal name.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Lewis Bayles Paton reads Esther as an unhistorical festival novella in which "the Agagite" echoes 1 Samuel 15 rather than proving an unbroken line from the historical Agag.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Lewis Bayles Paton (1908), A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Book of Esther (ICC).

sides.snippet: Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before Yahweh in Gilgal.
sides.verseText: Samuel said, As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless among women. Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before Yahweh in Gilgal.

sides.snippet: did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite
sides.verseText: After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes who were with him.
